column4: Several Host Discovery Commands From One Parent
column5: A burst of distinct discovery binaries from one parent; any tool set produces it; spacing the commands out evades it

column4: Failed Logons For Many Accounts From One Source
column5: One failed logon per account sprayed is inherent to the technique; a spray slower than the window evades it

column4: Kerberos Authentication Failures For Many Accounts From One Source
column5: Failed Kerberos pre-authentication per account is inherent to a Kerberos spray; a slow spray evades it

column4: RC Script Modified From The Command Line
column5: Writing an rc script is core to RC script persistence; a write from inside an interpreter that never names the file on a command line evades it

column4: Loaded Kernel Module Enumeration
column5: Keys on lsmod kmod modinfo and /proc/modules on a command line; a custom binary reading the module list evades it

column4: Shared Object Compiled With A Load-Time Initialiser
column5: Keys on the compiler and linker flag; a prebuilt library or a constructor attribute in source evades it

column4: Crypto Miner Indicators In Logs
column5: Miner binary names are adversary-brought; the stratum URL branch matches only when the pool URL is logged and a config file avoids that

column4: Host Log Enumeration
column5: Pre-existing tools (utmpdump lastlog) and literal cat command strings; another reader such as less evades the cat branch

column4: PAM Configuration Modification
column5: The /etc/pam.d path is core to the sub-technique but is ANDed with a list of editor and shell write verbs; another writer evades it

column4: Shadow File Read Attempt
column5: Reading /etc/shadow is core to the sub-technique with any tool; seen only when the path appears in an auth log line

column4: SSH Authorized Keys File Modification
column5: The authorized_keys path is core but is ANDed with a list of write tools; another writer evades it

column4: Systemd Timer Unit Creation Or Activation
column5: Keys on systemctl verbs with a .timer unit; enabling by creating the wants symlink directly evades it

column4: System Language And Location Discovery
column5: Pre-existing tools (reg query of Control\Nls and locale cmdlets); an API call from a custom binary evades it

column4: Wi-Fi Profile Enumeration Via Netsh
column5: Pre-existing tool netsh wlan show; the WLAN API from a custom binary evades it

column4: Diskshadow Script Mode - Execution From Potential Suspicious Location
column5: Pre-existing tool diskshadow with a script from a listed folder; another folder evades it

column4: Windows Defender Grace Period Expired
column5: An operating system event independent of the tool that caused it; one of several ways protection lapses

column4: PowerShell Script With File Hostname Resolving Capabilities
column5: Four literal strings of one script's content; rewriting the script evades it

column4: Potentially Suspicious Self Extraction Directive File Created
column5: The .sed directive is an artifact of the pre-existing IExpress tool; any extension change at creation evades it

column4: Failed Logon From Public IP
column5: Failed logon events from public sources are produced by any external guessing tool; internal sources are out of scope

column4: Registry Disable System Restore
column5: The policy value itself is matched whatever tool writes it; other ways to inhibit recovery evade it

column4: HackTool - EDRSilencer Execution - Filter Added
column5: Keys on the filter name one tool uses; renaming the filter evades it

column4: UAC Bypass via Event Viewer
column5: The mscfile open command key is core to this bypass whatever tool writes it

column4: Active Directory Computers Enumeration With Get-AdComputer
column5: Pre-existing cmdlet; a raw LDAP query evades it

column4: Potentially Suspicious Network Connection To Notion API
column5: The service endpoint is core to command and control over Notion; another web service evades it

column4: Processes Accessing the Microphone and Webcam
column5: Consent store object access is produced by any non-packaged program using the devices

column4: Potential Password Spraying Attempt Using Dsacls.EXE
column5: Pre-existing tool dsacls with credential arguments

column4: Remote Access Tool - Team Viewer Session Started On Linux Host
column5: Exact process names and command line of one remote access product

column5: Names and arguments of one offensive tool
